title: Keyboard Manager: Remapped Copilot key (F23) not recognized in Citrix Workspace session
author: Jrmewam

judgment.rationale: The latest discussion confirms that two local Copilot-key remappers work outside Citrix but fail in the native Citrix virtual desktop. This establishes a remote-input boundary, but not whether Citrix receives an injected Right Ctrl event or deliberately filters it.
evidence: The original report says the F23-based Copilot-key shortcut remap works locally but not in Citrix Workspace 25.8.10.36.
The reporter says Citrix TransparentKeyPassthrough=Local makes remapping work but prevents remote Alt+Tab.
The reporter later confirmed a separate Copilot-key remapper also fails in the Citrix virtual desktop.
The HTML5 Citrix session in Edge works, while Firefox and the native client do not.
Keyboard Manager injects remapped target input through its keyboard-hook pipeline; there is no Citrix-specific handling in the investigated area.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a focused native-Citrix versus HTML5 input comparison and Citrix keyboard redirection configuration before determining whether any supported PowerToys change is possible.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current evidence points to native Citrix keyboard virtualization accepting physical input differently from injected remapped input. No PowerToys code boundary is proven, and altering Citrix pass-through policy would be outside PowerToys ownership.

issue_context.summary: A Copilot-key-to-Right-Ctrl shortcut remap works on the local computer but is not recognized by a native Citrix Workspace virtual desktop, while the Citrix HTML5 session in Edge works.
known_information: The device is an LG Gram 2025 with a Copilot key reported as Left Win+Left Shift+F23.
The report names Citrix Workspace 25.8.10.36 and Windows 11 build 26200.7171.
The mapping works locally and in Citrix HTML5 through Edge.
Changing TransparentKeyPassthrough to Local restores remapping but sends Alt+Tab to the local desktop.
A second locally functioning Copilot-key remapper has the same native-Citrix limitation.
inferences: Citrix native-client keyboard redirection or virtual-channel policy may distinguish PowerToys-injected events from hardware events.
The successful Edge/HTML5 result makes an underlying general Keyboard Manager failure less likely, but does not rule it out.
issue_context.analysis: The new comments materially strengthen the third-party-boundary diagnosis but do not identify an actionable PowerToys defect. The next useful evidence is whether native Citrix receives the injected key at all under documented keyboard-redirection modes.
initial_investigation: Read the full live issue body and all six comments.
Reviewed the current Keyboard Manager event-dispatch and virtual-input boundary.
Searched live issues for a direct Citrix Copilot-key duplicate; this is the only matching open report.
Compared the HTML5 success and native-client failure described by the reporter.

information_gaps.information: A native Citrix-versus-HTML5 comparison showing whether physical Right Ctrl and the remapped Copilot key reach an in-session key tester under each documented keyboard-redirection mode.
information_gaps.why_needed: It determines whether Citrix filters injected events before the remote session, which would make this an external client-policy limitation rather than a PowerToys remap defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use a non-sensitive test desktop and key tester; record Citrix Workspace version, fullscreen/windowed mode, the documented keyboard-redirection setting, and results for physical Right Ctrl and the remapped key. Do not share organizational connection details.

comment.body: Thank you for confirming that the native Citrix client rejects the remapped key even when another local Copilot-key remapper is used, while Citrix HTML5 in Edge works. That points to native-client keyboard redirection rather than the local mapping alone. Please compare physical Right Ctrl and the remapped Copilot key in a non-sensitive in-session key tester for native Citrix (windowed and fullscreen) and Citrix HTML5, noting the documented keyboard-redirection mode. Do not include server, account, or company details. This will show whether Citrix filters injected input before it reaches the virtual desktop.
